data.Name: TP-05 | Scheduled Task/Job: Systemd Timers
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-05 Software Supply Chain / Source Code / CI-CD Compromise
data.Description: Create a systemd timer that periodically re-executes attacker code or checks for restored repository tokens. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Periodic persistence can survive temporary interruption and is relevant to self-hosted runners or Linux engineering workstations. Applicability: Linux Developer / Runner. Software supply-chain stage: Schedule Developer / Runner Persistence. Primary assets at risk: Linux runners, Developer systems. Attack-path stage: Schedule Developer / Runner Persistence. Detection opportunities: New user/system timers; Timer executing unusual scripts. Defensive considerations: Ephemeral runners; FIM; Audit systemd user services.

data.Description: Encode or encrypt scripts and payloads placed in workflows, packages or developer environments. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Obfuscation makes malicious dependency or pipeline modifications harder to identify in code review and static scanning. Applicability: Core. Software supply-chain stage: Obfuscate Malicious Pipeline / Package Payload. Primary assets at risk: Workflow scripts, Package payloads, Developer tools. Attack-path stage: Obfuscate Malicious Pipeline / Package Payload. Detection opportunities: High-entropy/encoded workflow content; Base64 decode-execute chains; Obfuscated package scripts. Defensive considerations: Static analysis; Code review; Block encoded execution patterns where feasible.

Defensive considerations: Package allow-listing; Provenance; FIM; Code signing.

data.Name: TP-05 | Execution Guardrails
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-05 Software Supply Chain / Source Code / CI-CD Compromise
data.Description: Check environment properties and execute only on selected developers, runners, organisations, regions or pipeline contexts. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Guardrails can reduce noisy detonation and make malicious packages appear benign during automated analysis while activating in targeted customer or development environments. Applicability: Conditional. Software supply-chain stage: Restrict Supply-Chain Payload Execution. Primary assets at risk: Developer endpoints, CI/CD runners, Targeted customer builds. Attack-path stage: Restrict Supply-Chain Payload Execution. Detection opportunities: Packages reading environment/locale before payload execution; Conditional network behavior. Defensive considerations: Sandbox diversity; Behavioral package testing; Detonate in representative CI/CD contexts.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-05 | Generic System Integrator / MSP software-supply-chain profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Guardrails can reduce noisy detonation and make malicious packages appear benign during automated analysis while activating in targeted customer or development environments. Threat-led context: No actor-specific evidence required for inclusion; technique is included because it is structurally relevant to the scenario. Applicability=Conditional; SupplyChainStage=Restrict Supply-Chain Payload Execution; Priority=Medium; Confidence=Medium. Scope boundary: TP-05 models compromise of developer identities, code repositories, CI/CD platforms and runners, package/dependency ecosystems, artifact/release processes, service connections, secrets, signing/authentication material and trusted software distribution. It includes both attacks against the organisation's development environment and abuse of that environment to compromise downstream customers. Generic identity compromise is covered in TP-01/TP-04, customer-side operations after malicious software reaches a customer belong to TP-03/TP-06, and full data-theft/exfiltration operations are expanded in TP-09. Conditional platform-specific records should be filtered against the actual development stack. This entry is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behavior has occurred.

data.Description: Check CPU, virtualization, environment or runner characteristics to avoid executing malicious behavior in analysis systems. Sandbox checks allow targeted malware to remain dormant until installed on real developer or customer systems. Applicability: Conditional. Attack-path stage: Evade Package / Pipeline Sandbox. Detection opportunities: Environment checks followed by conditional exit; Different behavior in analysis vs production. Defensive considerations: Multiple analysis profiles; Behavioral detonation; Production-like test runners.

Defensive considerations: EDR; DLP; Monitor runner archive creation.

data.Name: TP-05 | Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Code Repository
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-05 Software Supply Chain / Source Code / CI-CD Compromise
data.Description: Use a code-repository serviceâ€”potentially the victim's own GitHub/GitLab accountâ€”to store or exfiltrate stolen credentials and data. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Repository traffic may be trusted and allowed from developer and CI/CD systems. Attackers can exploit this trust by creating repositories or release assets that contain stolen data. Applicability: Core. Software supply-chain stage: Exfiltrate Through Repository Service. Primary assets at risk: GitHub/GitLab repositories, Release assets, Stolen credentials, Source data. Attack-path stage: Exfiltrate Through Repository Service. Detection opportunities: New public repository from CI token; Unexpected release asset uploads; Runner creating repository outside approved org structure. Defensive considerations: Restrict token repo-creation rights; Monitor public repositories; DLP for code platforms.

data.Description: Use HTTP/HTTPS to download payloads, communicate with C2 or exfiltrate secrets from developer and CI/CD environments. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Web traffic is routinely required for source control and package downloads, giving malicious web connections substantial camouflage. Applicability: Core. Attack-path stage: Use HTTPS from Pipeline / Developer Host. Detection opportunities: New domains contacted by runner; HTTP POST after secret collection; Typosquat security/tool domains. Defensive considerations: Egress proxy; Domain allow-listing for high-trust runners; TLS inspection where appropriate.

data.Description: Use a secondary channel such as a public repository when the primary exfiltration or command-and-control path is unavailable. Defensive considerations: Restrict repo creation; Monitor automation identities; Egress policy.

data.Name: TP-06 | Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Scan exposed VPN, firewall, remote-access, web, file-transfer, backup and enterprise applications for exploitable vulnerabilities. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Ransomware operations are highly opportunistic around internet-facing infrastructure. Mandiant found exploitation/suspected exploitation in about one-third of 2025 ransomware incidents, particularly VPNs and firewalls. Applicability: Internet-Facing. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Intrusion. Primary assets at risk: VPN gateways, Firewalls, Citrix, SharePoint, SAP, Managed file transfer, Backup software. Detection opportunities: WAF/IDS scanning signals; High-rate vulnerability probes; Repeated requests to known vulnerable endpoints. Defensive considerations: Rapid patching; External attack-surface management; Reduce direct exposure; WAF/IPS; CISA KEV prioritisation.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Ransomware operations are highly opportunistic around internet-facing infrastructure. Mandiant found exploitation/suspected exploitation in about one-third of 2025 ransomware incidents, particularly VPNs and firewalls. Threat-led context: Mandiant 2025 ransomware investigations: exploitation/suspected exploitation was the most common identified initial access vector. Applicability=Internet-Facing; RansomwarePhase=Pre-Intrusion; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | External Remote Services
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use stolen or brute-forced credentials to authenticate to VPN, Citrix, VNC, externally exposed management or other remote access services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Legitimate remote services are a frequent ransomware entry mechanism and may directly place the actor inside trusted network zones. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: VPN, Citrix, Remote support, Management gateways. Detection opportunities: New device/location; Successful login after brute force; Access outside normal hours; Remote session followed by reconnaissance. Defensive considerations: MFA; Source restrictions; Device compliance; Named accounts; No direct admin access from VPN.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Legitimate remote services are a frequent ransomware entry mechanism and may directly place the actor inside trusted network zones. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed stolen credentials commonly used against VPN/RDP. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Initial Access; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Trusted Relationship
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Leverage an already compromised supplier, subsidiary, MSP, partner or customer trust path to enter the target environment. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: System integrators have reciprocal third-party risk: they may be used to reach customers, but their own suppliers, subsidiaries or partner connectivity may also become an initial ransomware path. Applicability: System Integrator / MSP Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: Vendor VPN, Partner accounts, Subsidiary networks, Managed service trust. Detection opportunities: Third-party authentication anomalies; Supplier access outside scope; Cross-environment pivot patterns. Defensive considerations: Least privilege for suppliers; Time-bound access; Network segmentation; Third-party MFA; Periodic trust review.

data.Name: TP-06 | Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use compromised Entra/cloud accounts to access Microsoft 365, Azure and other SaaS/IaaS administration surfaces. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Modern ransomware can expand from identity compromise into cloud control planes, including cloud-native extortion and destructive actions. Applicability: Cloud / Entra. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Initial Access / Cloud Pivot. Primary assets at risk: Entra ID, Azure, Microsoft 365, Cloud storage, Cloud backups. Detection opportunities: SigninLogs; Risk detections; New cloud services accessed; Privileged API activity after risky login. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Conditional Access; PIM; Dedicated admin identities.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Modern ransomware can expand from identity compromise into cloud control planes, including cloud-native extortion and destructive actions. Threat-led context: Storm-0501 demonstrates ransomware/extortion operations extending into Entra and Azure. Applicability=Cloud / Entra; RansomwarePhase=Initial Access / Cloud Pivot; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Brute Force: Password Spraying
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Try common passwords across many enterprise identities to obtain a working VPN, cloud or domain account. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Spraying reduces per-account failure volume and remains relevant across identity providers and remote-access systems. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: Entra users, VPN users, Domain users. Detection opportunities: Many users targeted from common infrastructure; Distributed spray detection. Defensive considerations: MFA; Password protection; Smart lockout; Block legacy authentication.

data.Name: TP-06 | Brute Force: Credential Stuffing
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Reuse breached username/password combinations against corporate identity, VPN and SaaS services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Infostealer and breach-derived credentials can provide silent ransomware entry if passwords are reused. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: VPN, Entra, SaaS, Remote services. Detection opportunities: Leaked credential correlation; Unfamiliar sign-in properties. Defensive considerations: MFA; Unique passwords; Leak monitoring.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Infostealer and breach-derived credentials can provide silent ransomware entry if passwords are reused. Threat-led context: Mandiant notes stolen credentials may originate from infostealer logs and underground access markets. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Initial Access; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Phishing: Spearphishing Link

data.Description: Send links that lead to credential theft, malicious download, remote-support abuse or payload execution. data.Name: TP-06 | Phishing: Spearphishing via Service
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use Teams or another collaboration service to impersonate support and persuade a user to enable remote access or install a legitimate support tool. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Mandiant observed a 2025 intrusion leading to CLOP ransomware where an initial-access partner impersonated help desk staff through Teams and convinced the user to install Quick Assist. Applicability: Conditional. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: Microsoft Teams, Support channels, User endpoints. Detection opportunities: External/rare Teams sender; Quick Assist installation after chat; User-reported support impersonation. Defensive considerations: Restrict external collaboration; Verified help-desk procedures; Application control.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Mandiant observed a 2025 intrusion leading to CLOP ransomware where an initial-access partner impersonated help desk staff through Teams and convinced the user to install Quick Assist. Threat-led context: Observed by Mandiant in an intrusion that led to CLOP deployment. Applicability=Conditional; RansomwarePhase=Initial Access; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Remote Access Tools: Remote Desktop Software
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Install or abuse legitimate remote management software such as AnyDesk, ScreenConnect, Splashtop or similar tools. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: RMM tools are trusted, digitally signed and designed for administration, making them effective for resilient ransomware access and difficult to distinguish from support activity. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Foothold / Persistence. Primary assets at risk: Endpoints, Servers, RMM consoles, Managed-service systems. Detection opportunities: New RMM installation; Remote session outside approved ticket/change; New operator/source. Defensive considerations: Allow-list approved RMM; MFA; Session logging; Application control; Tie sessions to tickets.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: RMM tools are trusted, digitally signed and designed for administration, making them effective for resilient ransomware access and difficult to distinguish from support activity. Threat-led context: Mandiant saw RMM in roughly 24% of 2025 incidents; Qilin uses remote desktop software. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Foothold / Persistence; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Create Account: Domain Account
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Create a domain account and grant it privileges for persistent access. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Ransomware operators commonly create or modify domain accounts after initial entry, sometimes adding them to highly privileged groups. Applicability: AD / Hybrid. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Foothold / Persistence. Primary assets at risk: Active Directory, Domain accounts, Privileged groups. Detection opportunities: New domain user; Account creation followed by admin membership. Defensive considerations: PAM/JIT; Provisioning governance; Alert on privileged account creation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Create Account: Cloud Account
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Create a new cloud identity for access that survives remediation of the initially compromised account. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Cloud ransomware/extortion actors may create independent identities once tenant privilege has been obtained. Applicability: Cloud. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Foothold / Cloud Persistence. Primary assets at risk: Entra ID, Cloud administrative accounts. Detection opportunities: New user outside lifecycle process; New account immediately assigned privilege. Defensive considerations: Identity governance; PIM; Alert on privileged user creation.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Cloud ransomware/extortion actors may create independent identities once tenant privilege has been obtained. Threat-led context: Relevant to ransomware actors extending compromise into cloud identity. Applicability=Cloud; RansomwarePhase=Foothold / Cloud Persistence; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed service-based ransomware execution. Applicability=Windows; RansomwarePhase=Deployment / Persistence; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Create Run/RunOnce registry entries or startup persistence for ransomware or precursors. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Registry autostart can ensure payload execution across reboot or multiple systems and is documented for Qilin/Agenda activity. Applicability: Windows. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Persistence / Deployment. Primary assets at risk: Windows endpoints, Servers. Detection opportunities: New Run/RunOnce entries; Payload launched from Public/Temp/AppData. Defensive considerations: Registry monitoring; EDR; Application control.

data.Name: TP-06 | Domain or Tenant Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Modify Group Policy to push scheduled tasks, scripts, security exclusions or ransomware across domain systems. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: GPO provides an enterprise-scale deployment mechanism and can simultaneously weaken defenses and execute ransomware. Applicability: AD / Hybrid. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Privilege / Deployment. Primary assets at risk: Active Directory, Group Policy, Windows fleet. Detection opportunities: GPO modification; New scheduled task policy; Defender settings changed through GPO. Defensive considerations: Tier 0 administration; GPO change approval; Alert on GPO modifications.

data.Name: TP-06 | Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Credentials
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Add attacker-controlled secret/certificate to an application, service principal or cloud identity. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This can preserve cloud control even after the initial human identity is reset and can support later destructive cloud actions. Applicability: Cloud. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Cloud Persistence. Primary assets at risk: Service principals, Applications, Automation identities. Detection opportunities: New app credential; Certificate/secret addition after risky sign-in. Defensive considerations: Workload identity federation; Managed identities; Alert on credential changes.

data.Name: TP-06 | Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Roles
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Grant attacker-controlled identities additional Entra or Azure roles. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Cloud privilege expansion can expose backup, storage, identity and compute administration required for ransomware or destructive extortion. Applicability: Cloud. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Cloud Privilege Escalation. Primary assets at risk: Entra roles, Azure RBAC, Cloud administrators. Detection opportunities: New Global Admin/Owner/Contributor assignment; Role change after risky sign-in. Defensive considerations: PIM; Approval; Least privilege; Alert on role assignment.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Cloud privilege expansion can expose backup, storage, identity and compute administration required for ransomware or destructive extortion. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to ransomware / enterprise disruption even where no specific current actor evidence is required. Applicability=Cloud; RansomwarePhase=Cloud Privilege Escalation; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

Defensive considerations: Least privilege; UAC hardening; EDR.

data.Name: TP-06 | Access Token Manipulation
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Manipulate or impersonate access tokens to execute with another user's or elevated security context. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Token manipulation can provide local privilege needed for credential dumping, defense impairment and ransomware deployment. Applicability: Windows. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Privilege Escalation. Primary assets at risk: Windows security tokens, Administrator sessions. Detection opportunities: Token impersonation/theft telemetry; Unexpected elevated process context. Defensive considerations: Credential isolation; Least privilege; EDR.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Token manipulation can provide local privilege needed for credential dumping, defense impairment and ransomware deployment. Threat-led context: MITRE documents Qilin using an embedded Mimikatz module for token manipulation. Applicability=Windows; RansomwarePhase=Privilege Escalation; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Read LSASS process memory to recover credentials, hashes or secrets from logged-on users. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Mandiant consistently observed LSASS dumping in ransomware incidents; it is a direct route to domain and administrative credentials. Detection opportunities: LSASS access; Credential dumping alerts; Mimikatz-like behavior. Defensive considerations: Credential Guard; PAW; EDR; Prevent privileged logon to lower tiers.

data.Name: TP-06 | OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Export or read SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY registry data to obtain local password hashes and secrets. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Local credential dumping supports lateral movement and can expose reused administrator passwords. Applicability: Windows. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Credential Access. Primary assets at risk: SAM, SYSTEM hive, SECURITY hive, Local administrators. Detection opportunities: reg save of SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY; Shadow-copy access to registry hives. Defensive considerations: LAPS; Credential Guard; EDR.

data.Name: TP-06 | OS Credential Dumping: NTDS
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Copy or access NTDS.dit to recover domain credential material. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: The AD database provides enterprise-scale credential access and can enable domain-wide ransomware deployment. Applicability: Active Directory. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Credential Access. Primary assets at risk: NTDS.dit, Domain controller, Domain credentials. Detection opportunities: NTDS access/copy; Volume shadow creation on DC; Unexpected backup privilege use. Defensive considerations: Tier 0 protection; DC hardening; EDR/MDI.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: The AD database provides enterprise-scale credential access and can enable domain-wide ransomware deployment. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed copying NTDS.dit in 2025 ransomware incidents. Applicability=Active Directory; RansomwarePhase=Credential Access; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | OS Credential Dumping: DCSync
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Abuse AD replication privileges to retrieve credential data including highly privileged account hashes. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: DCSync can convert elevated directory privilege into domain-wide credential compromise without touching LSASS on the DC. Applicability: Active Directory. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Credential Access. Primary assets at risk: Domain controller replication, KRBTGT, Domain admins. Detection opportunities: Replication requests from non-DC; Unusual replication rights. Defensive considerations: Restrict replication privileges; MDI; Tier 0 governance.

data.Name: TP-06 | Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Request service tickets and crack them offline to obtain service-account passwords. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Over-privileged service accounts can become escalation paths to servers, backups and deployment systems. Applicability: Active Directory. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Credential Access. Primary assets at risk: Service accounts, SPNs, Privileged application accounts. Detection opportunities: High-volume TGS requests; RC4 service tickets where unexpected. Defensive considerations: gMSA; Long random passwords; AES; Least privilege.

data.Name: TP-06 | Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Extract browser-saved credentials, cookies or DPAPI-protected secrets from Chromium-based browsers. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Ransomware actors may recover privileged or SaaS credentials stored by administrators and users. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Credential Access. Primary assets at risk: Chrome, Edge, Browser profiles. Detection opportunities: Credential database access; Browser Local State decryption activity. Defensive considerations: Disable storage of privileged passwords; EDR; PAW.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Ransomware actors may recover privileged or SaaS credentials stored by administrators and users. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed browser credential recovery using DPAPI. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Credential Access; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Description: Access enterprise or user password managers to obtain administrative, customer and infrastructure credentials. Detection opportunities: Vault export; New device accessing vault; Database extraction. Defensive considerations: Enterprise PAM; Hardware-backed MFA; Restrict export; Monitor vault access.

data.Description: Retrieve secrets from Azure Key Vault or equivalent stores using a compromised privileged identity. data.Description: Enumerate Domain Admins and other privileged AD groups. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Domain-wide ransomware deployment often requires or benefits from privileged group membership. Applicability: Active Directory. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Discovery. Primary assets at risk: Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Backup admins, Server admins. Detection opportunities: Group membership enumeration; PowerShell/LDAP bulk queries. Defensive considerations: Monitor privilege discovery; Tier 0 controls.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Domain-wide ransomware deployment often requires or benefits from privileged group membership. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed Domain Admin enumeration; Qilin enumerates domain groups. Applicability=Active Directory; RansomwarePhase=Discovery; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Network Service Discovery
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Scan internal systems for RDP, SMB, SSH, vCenter, databases and other reachable services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Service discovery selects lateral-movement routes and identifies virtualization, backup and file servers. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Internal Reconnaissance. Primary assets at risk: RDP, SMB, SSH, vCenter, Databases, Management interfaces. Detection opportunities: Port scanning; Sequential destination/service probing. Defensive considerations: Segmentation; East-west monitoring; Management-plane enclaves.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Service discovery selects lateral-movement routes and identifies virtualization, backup and file servers. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed public network scanning tools in ~50% of ransomware intrusions. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Internal Reconnaissance; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Network Share Discovery
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Enumerate SMB/network shares and mounted resources. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Shares are prime ransomware targets because they concentrate business data and provide a mechanism for mass encryption or staging. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Internal Reconnaissance. Primary assets at risk: File shares, Admin shares, NAS, Mapped drives. Detection opportunities: net view / ShareFinder / SMB enumeration. Defensive considerations: Share ACL least privilege; Segmentation; Monitor enumeration.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. data.Name: TP-06 | Software Discovery: Backup Software Discovery
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Enumerate backup software, services, configuration and recovery tooling such as Veeam, Commvault or Cohesity. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Backup systems are ransomware crown jewels. Actors discover them to steal credentials, delete backups and prevent recovery. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Impact Discovery. Primary assets at risk: Veeam, Commvault, Cohesity, Backup agents, Recovery consoles. Detection opportunities: Queries for backup products/services; Registry/process inspection targeting backup software. Defensive considerations: Isolate backup plane; Separate backup identities; Immutable backups; Alert on backup discovery.

data.Name: TP-06 | System Service Discovery
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Enumerate system services to identify security, backup, database and business services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Service discovery precedes stopping services so files can be encrypted and protections disabled. Applicability: Windows / Linux. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Impact Discovery. Primary assets at risk: Windows/Linux services, Backup agents, Databases. Detection opportunities: sc query / Get-Service / systemctl enumeration. Defensive considerations: Behavioral detection.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Service discovery precedes stopping services so files can be encrypted and protections disabled. Threat-led context: Qilin performs system service discovery. Applicability=Windows / Linux; RansomwarePhase=Pre-Impact Discovery; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Cloud Service Discovery
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Enumerate cloud services available to compromised ransomware identities. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Cloud service discovery identifies storage, compute, backups and identity capabilities that can be targeted for extortion or destruction. Applicability: Cloud. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Cloud Discovery. Primary assets at risk: Azure, M365, Cloud backup, Storage. Detection opportunities: Rapid service enumeration; New cloud service access after identity compromise. Defensive considerations: Least privilege; Behavior analytics.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Cloud service discovery identifies storage, compute, backups and identity capabilities that can be targeted for extortion or destruction. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to ransomware / enterprise disruption even where no specific current actor evidence is required. Applicability=Cloud; RansomwarePhase=Cloud Discovery; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Cloud Storage Object Discovery
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Enumerate files and objects in cloud storage to select data for theft, encryption or deletion. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Cloud-native ransomware may act directly on storage without deploying a conventional endpoint encryptor. Applicability: Cloud. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Cloud Discovery. Primary assets at risk: Azure Storage, OneDrive, Cloud object storage, Backups. Detection opportunities: Mass object listing; Enumeration followed by bulk read/write/delete. Defensive considerations: Storage least privilege; Versioning/immutability; Monitor mass operations.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Cloud-native ransomware may act directly on storage without deploying a conventional endpoint encryptor. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to ransomware / enterprise disruption even where no specific current actor evidence is required. Applicability=Cloud; RansomwarePhase=Cloud Discovery; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol

data.Description: Use compromised or attacker-created accounts to move interactively between Windows systems. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: RDP was observed by Mandiant in approximately 85% of 2025 ransomware intrusions, making it one of the most important lateral-movement techniques in this profile. Detection opportunities: RDP from new sources; Admin account accessing many hosts; Off-hours RDP. Defensive considerations: MFA/gateway; Segmentation; PAW; Limit RDP.

data.Name: TP-06 | Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use SMB and administrative shares to access remote systems, stage ransomware and execute commands. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: SMB is widely used for ransomware payload staging and mass deployment across Windows networks. Applicability: Core / Windows. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Lateral Movement / Deployment. Primary assets at risk: SMB shares, ADMIN$, C$, File servers. Detection opportunities: Admin-share access from unusual hosts; Mass file copy; SMBEXEC/PsExec patterns. Defensive considerations: Segmentation; Disable unnecessary SMB; Admin share monitoring.

data.Name: TP-06 | Remote Services: SSH
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use SSH to move to Linux servers, appliances and ESXi hypervisors. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Mandiant observed PuTTY/KiTTY and SSH as common routes to ESXi before ransomware deployment. Applicability: Linux / ESXi. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Lateral Movement / Virtualization. Primary assets at risk: Linux, ESXi, Appliances. Detection opportunities: New SSH source/key; root login from unusual host; SSH enabled immediately before access. Defensive considerations: Management VLAN; Short-lived keys; MFA where possible; No shared root credentials.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. data.Description: Exploit vulnerabilities in internal services to gain access to additional systems. data.Name: TP-06 | Lateral Tool Transfer
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Transfer ransomware encryptors, scanning tools, scripts or C2 utilities between systems. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Enterprise-wide deployment requires moving tools to target servers, endpoints and hypervisors. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Deployment. Primary assets at risk: Endpoints, Servers, ESXi, Domain controllers. Detection opportunities: Executable copied to many hosts; SMB/SCP transfer shortly before execution. Defensive considerations: EDR; File reputation; Admin share monitoring.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Enterprise-wide deployment requires moving tools to target servers, endpoints and hypervisors. Threat-led context: Qilin uses PsExec for lateral tool transfer; Mandiant saw SMB/SCP staging. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Deployment; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use shell commands to stage, configure and execute ransomware on Linux, NAS or hypervisor systems. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Cross-platform ransomware operations increasingly target Linux and virtualization infrastructure. Applicability: Linux / ESXi. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Execution / Virtualization. Primary assets at risk: Linux, NAS, ESXi. Detection opportunities: Shell execution from unusual admin session; Encryption binary launch. Defensive considerations: Shell audit; Management-plane isolation; EDR where available.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Cross-platform ransomware operations increasingly target Linux and virtualization infrastructure. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed Linux ransomware and ESXi operations; Qilin supports Linux/ESXi. Applicability=Linux / ESXi; RansomwarePhase=Execution / Virtualization; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Command and Scripting Interpreter: Cloud API
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use Microsoft Graph, Azure APIs, CLI or PowerShell modules with privileged cloud identities. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Cloud-native ransomware can steal data, alter identity, delete backups and manipulate storage entirely through legitimate APIs. Applicability: Cloud. Detection opportunities: Unusual destructive API sequences; Bulk delete/write after privilege escalation. Defensive considerations: PIM; API behavior analytics; Protected backup roles.

data.Name: TP-06 | Command and Scripting Interpreter: Hypervisor CLI
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use hypervisor command-line interfaces such as esxcli or vim-cmd to enumerate VMs, change security settings, stop workloads and execute ransomware. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: The hypervisor management plane provides exceptional blast radius and is increasingly targeted in ransomware deployments. Applicability: Virtualization. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Virtualization Deployment. Primary assets at risk: ESXi, vCenter, VMware management. Detection opportunities: esxcli/vim-cmd from new admin/source; ExecInstalledOnly changes; VM shutdown commands. Defensive considerations: Isolate hypervisor management; Dedicated credentials; MFA through vCenter where possible; Command auditing.

data.Name: TP-06 | Ingress Tool Transfer
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Download scanners, tunnelers, RMM installers, exfiltration tools or ransomware payloads from external sources. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Ransomware operators frequently retrieve commodity tools only after entering the network. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Tooling. Primary assets at risk: Endpoints, Servers, ESXi, NAS. Detection opportunities: curl/wget/PowerShell downloads; New executable from public hosting. Defensive considerations: Egress filtering; Web reputation; Application control.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Ransomware operators frequently retrieve commodity tools only after entering the network. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed downloads of Rclone and ransomware payloads using wget/curl. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Tooling; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use HTTP/HTTPS for C2, downloads or data transfer. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Web protocols blend with normal enterprise traffic and support both custom malware and public tunneling frameworks. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Command and Control. Primary assets at risk: Endpoints, Servers, Proxy, Internet. Detection opportunities: Periodic HTTPS from non-browser process; New domains; Large POST after staging. Defensive considerations: Proxy; TLS/domain monitoring; Egress allow-list for critical servers.

data.Name: TP-06 | Application Layer Protocol: File Transfer Protocols
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use FTP/SFTP/SCP clients such as WinSCP, FileZilla or PuTTY SCP to transfer tools or stolen data. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Mandiant observed legitimate FTP/SFTP clients in 26% of incidents with confirmed/suspected data theft; Qilin uses WinSCP for Linux payload transfer. Detection opportunities: New FTP/SFTP process; Large outbound transfer; SCP to ESXi. Defensive considerations: Egress controls; Allow-list approved transfer tools; DLP.

data.Name: TP-06 | Proxy: Internal Proxy
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Proxy traffic through compromised hosts to reach restricted internal resources. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Ransomware actors use tunnelers to bridge segmented networks and hide the true source of lateral access. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Command and Control / Lateral. Primary assets at risk: Internal network, Management zones, Remote services. Detection opportunities: Unexpected listener/proxy process; New internal forwarding path. Defensive considerations: Segmentation; Egress controls; EDR.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Ransomware actors use tunnelers to bridge segmented networks and hide the true source of lateral access. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed multiple tunnelers including Chisel, Cloudflared and private tools. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Command and Control / Lateral; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Disable or Modify Tools
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Terminate, disable, exclude or reconfigure security tools so ransomware can execute without interruption. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Defense impairment is a consistent pre-encryption action. Ransomware operators commonly disable Defender, EDR and other security products before deployment. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Impact Defense Impairment. Primary assets at risk: EDR, Antivirus, Monitoring agents, Security tools. Detection opportunities: Security service termination; Policy/exclusion changes; Tamper events. Defensive considerations: Tamper protection; Separate security admin; PIM; Alert on agent health.

data.Name: TP-06 | Disable or Modify Tools: Disable or Modify Cloud Log
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Disable or alter cloud logging and audit integrations before destructive cloud actions. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Cloud-native ransomware benefits from reducing evidence of storage, backup and identity manipulation. Applicability: Cloud. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Cloud Defense Impairment. Primary assets at risk: Entra audit, Azure diagnostic settings, SIEM export, M365 audit. Detection opportunities: Audit configuration changes; Log ingestion gap; Admin disabling diagnostic settings. Defensive considerations: Separate log admin; Protected external SIEM; Alert on logging changes.

data.Name: TP-06 | Disable or Modify System Firewall

data.Description: Disable or modify system firewall controls to permit RDP, SMB, SSH, tunneling or malware traffic. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Mandiant observed attackers changing firewall rules to enable remote services and disabling ESXi firewalls before ransomware operations. Detection opportunities: Firewall disable/change; New RDP/SSH allow rule; Change by unusual admin. Defensive considerations: Protect management networks; Alert on firewall changes; Configuration enforcement.

data.Name: TP-06 | Safe Mode Boot
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Force Windows into Safe Mode so third-party security tools may not start before ransomware execution. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Safe Mode is a known ransomware defense-impairment technique and is currently represented as T1688 in ATT&CK v19. Applicability: Windows. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Impact Defense Impairment. Primary assets at risk: Windows endpoints, EDR. Detection opportunities: BCD Safe Mode changes; Unexpected Safe Mode reboot; Ransomware execution after reboot. Defensive considerations: Protect BCD changes; EDR tamper protection; Alert on safe mode configuration.

data.Name: TP-06 | Masquerading: Masquerade Task or Service
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Give malicious tasks or services benign-looking names to resemble legitimate update or support components. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Ransomware operators use familiar Microsoft/support naming to make persistence and defense-impairment tasks less suspicious. Applicability: Windows. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Stealth. Primary assets at risk: Scheduled tasks, Windows services. Detection opportunities: Task/service names inconsistent with binaries; New task named like update/support software. Defensive considerations: Baseline tasks/services; EDR.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Ransomware operators use familiar Microsoft/support naming to make persistence and defense-impairment tasks less suspicious. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed benign task names; Qilin mimics TeamViewer task names. Applicability=Windows; RansomwarePhase=Stealth; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Execution Guardrails: Mutual Exclusion
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use a mutex or equivalent mechanism so only one ransomware instance runs. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Mutual exclusion reduces execution errors and can be used as a recognizable ransomware implementation behavior. Applicability: Ransomware Payload. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Payload Execution. Primary assets at risk: Ransomware process, Host. Detection opportunities: Known/random mutex creation correlated with encryption. Defensive considerations: Behavioral detection.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Mutual exclusion reduces execution errors and can be used as a recognizable ransomware implementation behavior. Threat-led context: Qilin and Storm-0501-associated ransomware families use mutual exclusion. Applicability=Ransomware Payload; RansomwarePhase=Payload Execution; Priority=Medium; Confidence=Medium. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

Defensive considerations: Behavioral sandboxing; EDR.

data.Name: TP-06 | Inhibit System Recovery
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Delete shadow copies, backups, snapshots, recovery catalogs or otherwise render recovery infrastructure unavailable. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This is a defining ransomware technique. Recovery denial increases operational pressure and ransom leverage; backup infrastructure is deliberately targeted before encryption. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Anti-Recovery / Impact. Primary assets at risk: VSS, Backup repositories, Snapshots, Veeam, Commvault, Cohesity, vCenter backups. Detection opportunities: VSS deletion; Backup-volume deletion; Snapshot deletion; Backup service/console changes. Defensive considerations: Immutable/offline backups; Separate backup identity; MFA/PAM; Recovery tests; Network isolation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Service Stop
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Stop services and processes so files become encryptable, defenses are disabled and business services become unavailable. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Ransomware may stop Exchange, SQL, backup agents, EDR or VM-related processes before encryption. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Impact / Impact. Primary assets at risk: Databases, Backup services, Security services, Business applications, VMs. Detection opportunities: Mass service stop; Security/backup/database services stopped before file modifications. Defensive considerations: Service protection; EDR; Alert on critical service stop.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Ransomware may stop Exchange, SQL, backup agents, EDR or VM-related processes before encryption. Threat-led context: ATT&CK explicitly links Service Stop with ransomware; Qilin and current ransomware operations stop services. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Pre-Impact / Impact; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | System Shutdown/Reboot
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Shutdown or reboot systems to force encryption states, stop VMs, lock BitLocker-encrypted hosts or increase disruption. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Mandiant observed automated VM shutdown and BitLocker deployments that scheduled reboot to force hosts into a locked state. Applicability: Core / Virtualization. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Impact / Impact. Primary assets at risk: Windows endpoints, Servers, Virtual machines, Hypervisors. Detection opportunities: Mass shutdown/reboot; Power-off via vCenter; Reboot shortly after BitLocker change. Defensive considerations: Alert on mass power actions; Separate virtualization admin; Change controls.

data.Name: TP-06 | Automated Collection
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Automate collection of legal, HR, accounting, business development, customer and technical data. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Double extortion makes data theft part of the ransomware threat model; Mandiant saw confirmed/suspected theft in 77% of 2025 ransomware intrusions. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Collection. Primary assets at risk: File servers, SharePoint, Email, Databases, Sensitive documents. Detection opportunities: High-volume file access; Bulk recursive copy/search. Defensive considerations: DLP; Least privilege; Behavior analytics.

data.Name: TP-06 | Data from Local System
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Collect sensitive files from compromised endpoints and servers. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Local systems may hold legal, HR, finance, project and customer data useful for extortion. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Collection. Primary assets at risk: Endpoints, Servers, Local project data. Detection opportunities: Mass local file reads; Archive creation after discovery. Defensive considerations: Endpoint DLP; Least privilege.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Local systems may hold legal, HR, finance, project and customer data useful for extortion. data.Name: TP-06 | Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use WinRAR, 7-Zip or other utilities to compress data before exfiltration. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: WinRAR use increased materially in 2025 ransomware incidents and is a common pre-exfiltration behavior. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Collection / Staging. Primary assets at risk: Sensitive data, Archives, Staging host. Detection opportunities: Large archive creation; Portable WinRAR/7z from admin path. Defensive considerations: DLP; EDR; Monitor archive utilities.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: WinRAR use increased materially in 2025 ransomware incidents and is a common pre-exfiltration behavior. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed WinRAR in roughly 23% of ransomware intrusions and common archiving before exfiltration. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Collection / Staging; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only.
