data.Name: TP-06 | Automated Exfiltration
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Automatically transfer selected file types or staged archives to attacker infrastructure. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Automation shortens dwell time and enables large-scale double-extortion theft before encryption. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Exfiltration. Primary assets at risk: Sensitive documents, Archives. Detection opportunities: Scripted recurring transfer; File-extension-filtered exfiltration. Defensive considerations: DLP; Network egress control.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Automation shortens dwell time and enables large-scale double-extortion theft before encryption. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed scripted Rclone transfers selecting common file extensions. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Exfiltration; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Delete Cloud Instance

data.Description: Delete cloud VMs or instances after malicious activity or as part of destructive impact. Defensive considerations: Resource locks; PIM; Protected recovery; Alert on delete.

data.Name: TP-06 | Data Encrypted for Impact
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Encrypt files, virtual disks, cloud storage objects or entire systems to deny availability and extort payment. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This is the defining ransomware impact technique. Current ATT&CK includes traditional hosts, ESXi VMFS datastores and cloud-storage object encryption. Qilin supports Windows, Linux and ESXi. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Impact. Primary assets at risk: Endpoints, Servers, File shares, ESXi datastores, Cloud storage, Databases. Detection opportunities: High-rate file rewrites/renames; VM disk encryption; Cloud object rewrite/encryption; BitLocker mass enablement. Defensive considerations: Ransomware protection; Immutable backups; Segmentation; EDR; Storage versioning.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: This is the defining ransomware impact technique. Current ATT&CK includes traditional hosts, ESXi VMFS datastores and cloud-storage object encryption. Qilin supports Windows, Linux and ESXi. Threat-led context: Qilin encrypts Windows/Linux/ESXi; Mandiant saw native BitLocker abuse; ATT&CK detects cloud object encryption. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Impact; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Account Access Removal
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Disable, delete or reset legitimate administrator accounts to delay containment and recovery. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Identity lockout can protect attacker persistence, block responders and amplify business outage during ransomware or cloud extortion. Applicability: Cloud / Identity / AD. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Impact / Response Inhibition. Primary assets at risk: Global admins, Domain admins, Security responders, Backup administrators. Detection opportunities: Privileged account disable/delete; Bulk password reset; Role removal. Defensive considerations: Emergency-access accounts; Out-of-band recovery; Alert on admin removal.

data.Name: TP-07 | Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Obtain leaked, infostealer-derived or previously compromised credentials for employees, executives, finance staff, help-desk personnel and administrators. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: BEC and identity-first phishing operations frequently begin with credential intelligence. For a system integrator, identities may also expose customer conversations, privileged access paths and trusted business relationships. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Targeting. Primary assets at risk: Employee identities, Finance identities, Executives, Help desk, Cloud administrators. Detection opportunities: Leaked credential monitoring; Identity Protection risk signals; Credential exposure correlation. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Credential exposure response; No password reuse.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: BEC and identity-first phishing operations frequently begin with credential intelligence. For a system integrator, identities may also expose customer conversations, privileged access paths and trusted business relationships. Threat-led context: Current identity-centric extortion operations rely heavily on stolen or socially engineered credentials. Applicability=Core; Phase=Targeting; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. It intentionally includes both classic BEC and modern identity-first phishing that may never deploy malware. Generic Entra identity compromise is expanded in TP-01, privileged-access compromise in TP-04, ransomware impact in TP-06 and full SaaS/data-theft extortion in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Description: Collect corporate email addresses for employees, executives, finance, HR, help desk, sales and technical personnel. data.Description: Identify named employees whose role, authority or customer relationships can make a phishing pretext believable. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: BEC succeeds through trust and context. Knowing names, reporting lines and customer-facing personnel allows attackers to impersonate credible senders and target users capable of approving financial or security-sensitive actions. Detection opportunities: User-reported impersonation; Brand monitoring. Defensive considerations: Limit unnecessary publication of sensitive roles; Security awareness for high-risk functions.

data.Name: TP-07 | Gather Victim Org Information: Business Relationships
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Research customers, suppliers, partners, MSP relationships and other trusted business connections that can be impersonated or compromised. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Business relationships are especially valuable against a system integrator because users expect frequent external communications and may trust messages from customers, Microsoft, vendors, accountants, recruiters and project partners. Applicability: System Integrator Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Targeting. Primary assets at risk: Customer relationships, Supplier relationships, Partner ecosystem, Managed-service relationships. Detection opportunities: Threat-intel monitoring for partner impersonation; Look-alike domain monitoring. Defensive considerations: Out-of-band verification for sensitive supplier/customer requests; External sender labelling.

data.Name: TP-07 | Gather Victim Org Information: Identify Business Tempo
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Identify payroll cycles, invoice timing, quarter-end activity, travel periods, executive absences and operational hours. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: BEC actors exploit moments when urgent payment, payroll, invoice or executive requests appear normal. Microsoft observed payroll diversion and conversational BEC lures throughout Q2 2026. Applicability: BEC Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Targeting. Primary assets at risk: Finance process, Payroll, Accounts payable, Executive schedule. Detection opportunities: BEC campaign intelligence; Anomalous payment-request timing. Defensive considerations: Dual approval for payment changes; Out-of-band financial verification.

data.Name: TP-07 | Gather Victim Org Information: Identify Roles
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Identify personnel with authority over payments, payroll, MFA reset, identity administration, support, executive decisions or customer access. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Role targeting enables both classic BEC and modern identity compromise. Help-desk and privileged-role targeting can turn social engineering into tenant-wide access. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Targeting. Primary assets at risk: Finance, Payroll, Help desk, Global administrators, Executives, Customer administrators. Detection opportunities: Targeting intelligence; Repeated phishing against named roles. Defensive considerations: Role-specific awareness; Strong help-desk identity verification; Separate admin identities.

data.Name: TP-07 | Establish Accounts: Email Accounts
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Create disposable or long-lived email accounts used to impersonate executives, vendors, customers, recruiters or support personnel. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: BEC commonly begins from attacker-controlled email accounts rather than compromised corporate mailboxes, especially during initial conversational outreach. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Prepare Persona. Primary assets at risk: External email, Business trust, Finance workflows. Detection opportunities: Look-alike sender monitoring; Display-name impersonation detections. Defensive considerations: DMARC/SPF/DKIM; External sender labelling; Out-of-band verification.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Threat-led context: ATT&CK documents creation of email accounts for phishing, BEC and extortion operations. Applicability=Core; Phase=Prepare Persona; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. data.Name: TP-07 | Establish Accounts: Cloud Accounts
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Create cloud or collaboration accounts used to contact targets through Microsoft Teams, SaaS trials or other trusted services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Cross-tenant collaboration can make attacker messages appear more legitimate than unsolicited email and may bypass traditional email security controls. Applicability: Teams / SaaS Conditional. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Prepare Persona. Primary assets at risk: Microsoft Teams, Cloud collaboration, SaaS trial tenants. Detection opportunities: External tenant contact anomalies; New external domain/tenant messaging users. Defensive considerations: Restrict external collaboration; Tenant allow/block controls; User awareness.

data.Name: TP-07 | Compromise Accounts: Email Accounts
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Compromise a legitimate email account belonging to an employee, supplier, customer or business partner and use it for phishing or fraud. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Compromised mailboxes enable thread hijacking, relationship abuse and internal-looking messages. ATT&CK explicitly notes that compromised email accounts can evade reputation controls and exploit existing trust. Applicability: BEC Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Prepare Trusted Persona. Primary assets at risk: Corporate mailbox, Supplier/customer mailbox, Email threads. Detection opportunities: Impossible/unusual sign-in; New forwarding rules; Outbound phishing burst; Thread hijack anomalies. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Mailbox audit; Risk-based Conditional Access.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Defensive considerations: Defensive domain registration; Brand monitoring; Web filtering.

data.Name: TP-07 | Stage Capabilities: Install Digital Certificate
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Install valid TLS certificates on attacker-controlled phishing or AiTM infrastructure. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: HTTPS and valid certificates increase visual legitimacy and are expected by users on Microsoft/SSO-style login pages. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Prepare Phishing Infrastructure. Primary assets at risk: Credential-harvesting site, AiTM proxy. Detection opportunities: Certificate-transparency monitoring for look-alike domains. Defensive considerations: Brand monitoring; Block newly registered look-alike domains.

data.Name: TP-07 | Generate Content: Written Content
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Create convincing phishing messages, financial requests, payroll lures, help-desk scripts, reply-chain text and other written pretexts, potentially using AI. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: ATT&CK added this technique in 2026. BEC operators can use AI-assisted writing to mimic style, translate messages and sustain realistic conversations. Kali365 is specifically documented generating tailored responses to facilitate BEC. Applicability: Core / AI-Assisted. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Prepare Social Engineering. Primary assets at risk: Email content, Teams messages, Fraudulent financial requests, Help-desk narratives. Detection opportunities: Content/behavior anomaly analysis; Conversation-context review; User reporting. Defensive considerations: Out-of-band verification; Process controls rather than content-only trust; User awareness.

data.Name: TP-07 | Generate Content: Audio-Visual Content
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Create or manipulate voice, images or video to support executive, help-desk, recruiter or customer impersonation. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Synthetic voice and visual content can strengthen vishing and collaboration-based fraud, especially where staff rely on voice/video familiarity as an identity check. Applicability: AI-Assisted / Vishing. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Prepare Social Engineering. Primary assets at risk: Voice calls, Video calls, Profile images, Identity documents. Detection opportunities: User reports; Call verification failures. Defensive considerations: Independent verification of sensitive requests; Do not treat voice/video familiarity as authentication.

data.Description: Send a link to a cloned SSO/Microsoft/customer portal to collect credentials, MFA information or other actionable data. Primary assets at risk: Entra credentials, M365 identity, Customer credentials. Detection opportunities: URL click telemetry; New domain; Credential-phishing page detection. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Safe Links; Browser protection.

data.Name: TP-07 | Social Engineering: Email Spoofing
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Manipulate sender identity or email headers so messages appear to originate from an internal user, executive, supplier or trusted domain. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Email spoofing remains important where SPF/DKIM/DMARC or complex mail routing is weak or misconfigured. It can support payment fraud without needing an account takeover. Applicability: BEC Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Delivery / Stealth. Primary assets at risk: Corporate domain, Supplier/customer domains, Email recipients. Detection opportunities: SPF/DKIM/DMARC failures; Composite authentication anomalies; Direct Send anomalies. Defensive considerations: DMARC enforcement; SPF/DKIM; Secure mail routing; External sender labelling.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Applicability=BEC Core; Phase=Delivery / Stealth; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

Defensive considerations: Safe Attachments; Block risky formats; EDR.

data.Name: TP-07 | Phishing: Spearphishing via Service
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Deliver phishing, malware or support impersonation through Microsoft Teams, social media, personal messaging or other third-party services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Teams-based phishing grew throughout Q2 2026 and can bypass secure email gateways while benefiting from collaboration-platform trust. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: Microsoft Teams, SaaS messaging, Social platforms. Detection opportunities: External Teams sender/call; Message followed by download/RMM activity; Cross-tenant anomalies. Defensive considerations: External collaboration restrictions; Safe collaboration controls; User training.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Threat-led context: Microsoft observed increasing Teams phishing and help-desk impersonation in 2026. Applicability=Core; Phase=Initial Access; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | User Execution: Malicious Copy and Paste
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Trick the victim into copying/pasting a device code or command as part of a fake authentication, CAPTCHA, support or remediation flow. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: ATT&CK now maps Kali365 device-code authorization to this technique. Social engineering can cause the user to complete a legitimate authorization flow that grants attacker-controlled token access. Applicability: Current 2026. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: User Interaction / Authentication. Primary assets at risk: Browser, Device-code login, PowerShell/Run dialog, Entra identity. Detection opportunities: Device-code authentication after phishing; Clipboard-to-shell chain; Unusual device authorization. Defensive considerations: Block/restrict device-code auth where appropriate; Phishing-resistant MFA; User training.

data.Name: TP-07 | Adversary-in-the-Middle
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Proxy the victim's authentication interaction to the legitimate identity provider while intercepting credentials, MFA and session artifacts. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This is the core technical behavior behind modern AiTM phishing. ATT&CK maps Kali365 directly to T1557 for reverse-proxy phishing pages that intercept user sessions. Applicability: AiTM Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Credential / Session Capture. Primary assets at risk: SSO authentication, MFA, Entra session. Detection opportunities: Phishing-domain proxy behavior; Sign-in/session anomalies; Token/session reuse. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Token protection; Conditional Access.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: This is the core technical behavior behind modern AiTM phishing. ATT&CK maps Kali365 directly to T1557 for reverse-proxy phishing pages that intercept user sessions. Threat-led context: Kali365 is mapped by ATT&CK to T1557; UNC6671 performs live AiTM during vishing. Applicability=AiTM Core; Phase=Credential / Session Capture; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. It intentionally includes both classic BEC and modern identity-first phishing that may never deploy malware. Generic Entra identity compromise is expanded in TP-01, privileged-access compromise in TP-04, ransomware impact in TP-06 and full SaaS/data-theft extortion in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Steal Application Access Token
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Capture OAuth access/refresh tokens via AiTM, device-code authorization, malicious OAuth flow or compromised session. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Access tokens can provide Graph/M365/SaaS access without the user's password and are central to modern Microsoft 365 phishing-as-a-service. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Token Theft. Primary assets at risk: OAuth access token, Refresh token, Microsoft Graph, M365. Detection opportunities: Token use from unusual client/IP; Device-code auth anomalies; Consent/token issuance after phishing. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Restrict device-code auth where appropriate; Token revocation.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Access tokens can provide Graph/M365/SaaS access without the user's password and are central to modern Microsoft 365 phishing-as-a-service. Threat-led context: Kali365 is explicitly mapped to T1528 for OAuth access and refresh token theft. Applicability=Core; Phase=Token Theft; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. It intentionally includes both classic BEC and modern identity-first phishing that may never deploy malware. Generic Entra identity compromise is expanded in TP-01, privileged-access compromise in TP-04, ransomware impact in TP-06 and full SaaS/data-theft extortion in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

Defensive considerations: Session protection; Managed-device requirements; Rapid revocation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Generate repeated MFA prompts or synchronize a vishing interaction with MFA requests to induce approval. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: ATT&CK explicitly notes combining spearphishing voice with MFA request generation. Help-desk pretexts make unexpected MFA activity appear legitimate. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: MFA Bypass. Primary assets at risk: MFA, Entra identity, Privileged users. Detection opportunities: Repeated MFA prompts; Denied/expired requests; Prompt immediately after external call. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Number matching; User education.

Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. data.Name: TP-07 | Brute Force: Password Spraying
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Attempt common passwords across known corporate email identities. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Phishing target lists and exposed email addresses may also be used for low-and-slow password spraying, particularly against users without strong MFA. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Credential Acquisition. Primary assets at risk: Entra ID, M365, VPN. Detection opportunities: Distributed failed sign-ins across many users. Defensive considerations: MFA; Smart lockout; Password protection.

data.Name: TP-07 | Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Use the compromised cloud identity to access mailbox, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive and connected SaaS applications. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: BEC depends on the attacker appearing to be the legitimate user. Valid cloud accounts allow activity to blend with normal email and collaboration behavior. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Account Takeover. Primary assets at risk: Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, SaaS. Detection opportunities: SigninLogs; Risk detections; Unusual mailbox/SaaS activity. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Conditional Access; Risk-based session controls.

Inclusion rationale: BEC depends on the attacker appearing to be the legitimate user. Valid cloud accounts allow activity to blend with normal email and collaboration behavior. Applicability=Core; Phase=Account Takeover; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Hide Artifacts: Email Hiding Rules
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Create inbox rules that move, mark read or delete security alerts, legitimate replies or messages that might expose the fraud. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Email hiding rules let the attacker suppress MFA/security notifications and prevent the real user from seeing responses to fraudulent messages. Kali365 supports this directly. Applicability: BEC Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Stealth / Mailbox Control. Primary assets at risk: Mailbox rules, Security notifications, Customer/vendor replies. Detection opportunities: Rules deleting/moving security or financial messages; Hidden inbox rules. Defensive considerations: Mailbox-rule audit; Alert on delete/move rules for security keywords.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Email hiding rules let the attacker suppress MFA/security notifications and prevent the real user from seeing responses to fraudulent messages. Kali365 supports this directly. Threat-led context: Kali365 can modify email rules to delete notifications before the victim sees them. Applicability=BEC Core; Phase=Stealth / Mailbox Control; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. It intentionally includes both classic BEC and modern identity-first phishing that may never deploy malware. Generic Entra identity compromise is expanded in TP-01, privileged-access compromise in TP-04, ransomware impact in TP-06 and full SaaS/data-theft extortion in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Modify Authentication Process: Multi-Factor Authentication
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Add weaker factors, remove MFA requirements or alter authentication methods to preserve account access. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Controlling the victim's authentication methods makes password resets less effective and can protect attacker persistence. Applicability: Core. Detection opportunities: MFA method add/remove/reset; Privileged authentication policy change. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Strong identity proofing; Alert on auth-method changes.

data.Name: TP-07 | Modify Authentication Process: Conditional Access Policies
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Modify Conditional Access policy, exclusions or trusted locations after compromising an administrative identity. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: A high-privilege account takeover can turn a single BEC/identity compromise into broader persistent access by excluding attacker-controlled identities from strong controls. Applicability: Privileged BEC / Admin Compromise. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Identity Persistence. Primary assets at risk: Conditional Access, Admin identities, Trusted locations. Detection opportunities: CA policy change after risky sign-in; New exclusion/trusted location. Defensive considerations: PIM; Alert on policy changes; Protected emergency access.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: A high-privilege account takeover can turn a single BEC/identity compromise into broader persistent access by excluding attacker-controlled identities from strong controls. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to phishing/BEC/AiTM/social-engineering operations. Applicability=Privileged BEC / Admin Compromise; Phase=Identity Persistence; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. It intentionally includes both classic BEC and modern identity-first phishing that may never deploy malware. Generic Entra identity compromise is expanded in TP-01, privileged-access compromise in TP-04, ransomware impact in TP-06 and full SaaS/data-theft extortion in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Cloud Application Integration
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Create, consent to or abuse an OAuth/cloud application with mailbox, files or directory permissions. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: OAuth persistence can survive user password resets and provides Graph/API access for mail collection, internal phishing and SaaS data theft. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Application Persistence. Primary assets at risk: Enterprise applications, OAuth grants, Microsoft Graph, Mailbox. Detection opportunities: New app registration; Admin/user consent; High-risk scopes. Defensive considerations: Restrict user consent; Admin consent workflow; App governance.

data.Name: TP-07 | Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Roles
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Grant additional cloud roles to the compromised or attacker-created identity. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Role expansion can provide Exchange, application or directory administration that enables broader mailbox access and tenant-level phishing. Applicability: Privileged Compromise. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Privilege Expansion. Primary assets at risk: Entra roles, Exchange roles, Cloud admin. Detection opportunities: New role assignment; PIM/role audit. Defensive considerations: PIM; Approval; Least privilege.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Role expansion can provide Exchange, application or directory administration that enables broader mailbox access and tenant-level phishing. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to phishing/BEC/AiTM/social-engineering operations. Applicability=Privileged Compromise; Phase=Privilege Expansion; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. It intentionally includes both classic BEC and modern identity-first phishing that may never deploy malware. Generic Entra identity compromise is expanded in TP-01, privileged-access compromise in TP-04, ransomware impact in TP-06 and full SaaS/data-theft extortion in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Cloud Service Dashboard
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Use legitimate web dashboards to inspect account settings, applications, mailboxes and connected services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Interactive post-phishing activity often uses the same web interfaces as legitimate users and administrators. Applicability: Cloud. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Post-Compromise Discovery. Primary assets at risk: M365 admin portals, Entra, SaaS dashboards. Detection opportunities: New portal/device/location; Unusual admin navigation. Defensive considerations: Conditional Access; Managed devices; PIM.

data.Name: TP-07 | Internal Spearphishing

data.Description: Use a compromised employee mailbox or collaboration account to send phishing or fraudulent requests to other internal users. data.Name: TP-07 | Command and Scripting Interpreter: Cloud API
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Use Microsoft Graph, Exchange APIs, PowerShell or other cloud APIs to enumerate mailboxes, modify rules, collect data or send messages. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: API-driven activity scales BEC and data theft and can evade analysts focused only on interactive portal usage. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Cloud Execution. Primary assets at risk: Microsoft Graph, Exchange Online, SharePoint APIs. Detection opportunities: API calls from unusual user agents; PowerShell/Graph usage by ordinary user. Defensive considerations: API behavior analytics; Least privilege; App governance.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: API-driven activity scales BEC and data theft and can evade analysts focused only on interactive portal usage. Threat-led context: Kali365 uses Graph; UNC6671 uses Graph, Python requests and PowerShell for SaaS collection. Applicability=Core; Phase=Cloud Execution; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. It intentionally includes both classic BEC and modern identity-first phishing that may never deploy malware. Generic Entra identity compromise is expanded in TP-01, privileged-access compromise in TP-04, ransomware impact in TP-06 and full SaaS/data-theft extortion in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Email Collection: Local Email Collection
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Collect cached Outlook mail, PST/OST content or local email stores from a compromised endpoint. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Endpoint compromise via social engineering can expose local mail even if cloud access is constrained. Applicability: Endpoint Conditional. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Collection. Primary assets at risk: Outlook cache, PST/OST, Local email. Detection opportunities: Mass access to mail stores; PST/OST copy. Defensive considerations: Endpoint DLP; EDR; Disk encryption.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. data.Name: TP-07 | Automated Collection
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Use scripts or APIs to automatically harvest mail, files or high-value SaaS information. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Automation allows data theft at scale and reduces dwell time. UNC6671 uses scripted Graph/HTTP collection after vishing compromise. Applicability: Cloud. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Collection. Primary assets at risk: SharePoint, OneDrive, Email, SaaS. Detection opportunities: python-requests/PowerShell user agent; Rapid high-volume file access. Defensive considerations: Behavior analytics; API monitoring; DLP.

data.Name: TP-07 | Proxy
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Use reverse proxies or relay services between the victim and legitimate authentication services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: AiTM phishing infrastructure depends on proxying legitimate login traffic while retaining control of the client-facing session. ATT&CK maps Kali365 to Proxy. Applicability: AiTM Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Phishing Infrastructure / C2. Primary assets at risk: AiTM infrastructure, SSO login. Detection opportunities: Reverse-proxy fingerprints; Cloudflare/hosting infrastructure correlated with phishing domain. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Web filtering; Threat intelligence.

data.Name: TP-07 | Web Service
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Use Cloudflare Workers, Telegram or another web service for phishing hosting, redirects, administration or coordination. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Trusted web services provide resilient infrastructure and blend with expected outbound traffic. Kali365 uses Cloudflare Workers and Telegram. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Infrastructure / C2. Primary assets at risk: Web services, Phishing redirects, Campaign administration. Detection opportunities: Rare service usage from phishing context; Threat-intel correlation. Defensive considerations: Web filtering; SaaS governance.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Trusted web services provide resilient infrastructure and blend with expected outbound traffic. Kali365 uses Cloudflare Workers and Telegram. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to phishing/BEC/AiTM/social-engineering operations. Applicability=Core; Phase=Infrastructure / C2; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. It intentionally includes both classic BEC and modern identity-first phishing that may never deploy malware. Generic Entra identity compromise is expanded in TP-01, privileged-access compromise in TP-04, ransomware impact in TP-06 and full SaaS/data-theft extortion in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage

data.Description: Transfer stolen email, documents or SaaS exports to attacker-controlled cloud storage. data.Name: TP-07 | Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Send collected data through attacker-controlled web/C2 infrastructure. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Cloud identity compromise may lead directly to scripted data exfiltration and extortion without endpoint ransomware. Applicability: Follow-on Extortion. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Exfiltration. Primary assets at risk: Stolen business data. Detection opportunities: Large POST after SaaS collection; C2 process transferring archive. Defensive considerations: Egress monitoring; DLP.

data.Name: TP-07 | Financial Theft
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Use impersonation or compromised business email to induce fraudulent payments, payroll changes, gift-card purchases or other transfers. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This is the core impact technique for classic BEC. ATT&CK explicitly links impersonation and social engineering to financial theft. Applicability: BEC Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Fraud / Impact. Primary assets at risk: Accounts payable, Payroll, Corporate funds, Payment process. Detection opportunities: New beneficiary/payment detail; Urgent executive payment request; Payroll account change. Defensive considerations: Dual approval; Call-back verification; No payment-detail changes by email alone.

data.Name: TP-07 | Account Access Removal
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Change passwords, authentication methods or account state to deny legitimate users access after compromise. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Lockout may extend attacker dwell time and impede rapid mailbox recovery, especially after the attacker registers their own authentication method. Applicability: Privileged Account Takeover. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Response Inhibition. Primary assets at risk: Victim account, Help-desk recovery, Administrator access. Detection opportunities: Password/MFA changes followed by failed legitimate login; Account disable/reset. Defensive considerations: Emergency access; Identity recovery process; Alert on auth-method changes.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Lockout may extend attacker dwell time and impede rapid mailbox recovery, especially after the attacker registers their own authentication method. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to phishing/BEC/AiTM/social-engineering operations. Applicability=Privileged Account Takeover; Phase=Response Inhibition; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. It intentionally includes both classic BEC and modern identity-first phishing that may never deploy malware. Generic Entra identity compromise is expanded in TP-01, privileged-access compromise in TP-04, ransomware impact in TP-06 and full SaaS/data-theft extortion in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-08 | Gather Victim Network Information: DNS
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Enumerate corporate and customer-facing DNS records to identify VPN gateways, portals, APIs, project/support systems, mail services and administrative endpoints. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: DNS reveals the organisation's externally reachable service topology and can expose forgotten or business-unit-specific systems that are not consistently governed. Applicability: Core. Internet-facing compromise phase: External Reconnaissance. Primary assets at risk: Public DNS, VPN names, Support portals, Project portals, API endpoints, Admin portals. Detection opportunities: External attack-surface inventory; Passive DNS monitoring; Alert on unexpected new public records. Defensive considerations: Central DNS ownership; Remove stale records; Continuous attack-surface management.

data.Name: TP-08 | Gather Victim Host Information: Software
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Identify software and versions running on public services through banners, HTTP headers, TLS metadata, error pages, login portals and product-specific responses. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Version fingerprinting lets attackers match exposed products against known vulnerabilities and rapidly weaponize newly disclosed CVEs. Applicability: Core. Internet-facing compromise phase: External Reconnaissance. Primary assets at risk: VPN appliances, Firewalls, Jira/project portals, Service desks, Confluence, Web frameworks, Reverse proxies. Detection opportunities: Banner/version exposure review; ASM product fingerprinting; Unexpected legacy software. Defensive considerations: Suppress unnecessary version disclosure; Asset inventory; Rapid vulnerability management.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-08 | Generic System Integrator / MSP internet-facing-services profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Version fingerprinting lets attackers match exposed products against known vulnerabilities and rapidly weaponize newly disclosed CVEs. Threat-led context: Microsoft and CISA continue to document active exploitation of internet-facing edge and enterprise software. Applicability=Core; Phase=External Reconnaissance; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-08 models external reconnaissance, attack-surface discovery, exploitation of public-facing applications and edge appliances, abuse of VPN/remote access and valid public-service accounts, post-exploit command execution, web shell/server persistence, credential and token theft, privilege escalation, internal/cloud discovery, tunneling, lateral movement, data collection/exfiltration and selected service-impact actions. It is deliberately generic enough for VPNs, firewalls, web apps, APIs, project portals, Jira/Confluence-like platforms, service desks, RMM gateways and custom customer-facing applications. Product-specific CVEs are evidence/examples, not hard-coded requirements. Identity-only compromise is deeper in TP-01, trusted customer pivot in TP-03, privileged access in TP-04, software supply chain in TP-05, ransomware/destruction in TP-06 and data-theft depth in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-08 | Active Scanning: Wordlist Scanning
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Use wordlists and automated content discovery to find hidden administrative paths, backup files, APIs, old applications and exposed files. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Project portals, service desks and custom applications may expose undocumented routes or legacy components that are not visible from normal navigation. Applicability: Core. Internet-facing compromise phase: Active Reconnaissance. Primary assets at risk: Web applications, APIs, Admin paths, Backup/config files. Detection opportunities: High-volume 404/path enumeration; Directory brute forcing; API endpoint enumeration. Defensive considerations: WAF; Disable directory listing; Remove legacy content; Authentication on admin paths.

data.Name: TP-08 | Exploit Public-Facing Application
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Exploit a vulnerability or misconfiguration in an internet-facing application, firewall, VPN, project/support portal, API gateway or collaboration server to gain initial access. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This is the defining ATT&CK technique for TP-08. Public-facing applications and edge devices are repeatedly exploited by ransomware, espionage and data-theft actors because they bypass user interaction and often sit at privileged network boundaries. Applicability: Core. Internet-facing compromise phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: VPN/SSL-VPN, Firewalls, Reverse proxies, Web applications, APIs, Confluence/Jira-like systems, Service desk/project portals. Detection opportunities: Exploit signatures; Unexpected child process from service; Web shell/file creation; New admin/session after exploit. Defensive considerations: KEV-driven patching; WAF/IPS; Exposure reduction; Segmentation; Virtual patching.

data.Name: TP-08 | External Remote Services
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Use legitimate VPN, Citrix, VNC, externally reachable remote management or other remote access services with compromised credentials. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: ATT&CK explicitly identifies VPN and other remote gateways as initial-access and persistence mechanisms. In a system-integrator environment these services often provide direct paths to administration networks. Applicability: Core. Internet-facing compromise phase: Use Exposed Remote Access. Primary assets at risk: VPN, Citrix, VNC, Remote support gateways, Administrative access. Detection opportunities: Unusual login source/device; Access outside support hours; Successful login after failures. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Named accounts; Device compliance; Source restrictions; No direct Tier-0 access.

data.Name: TP-08 | Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Authenticate to internet-facing SaaS, support, project, identity or cloud administration services using a valid compromised cloud account. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Internet-facing SaaS does not require vulnerability exploitation; stolen credentials or sessions can provide direct access to project, ticketing, customer and administrative data. Applicability: Cloud / SaaS. Internet-facing compromise phase: Use Exposed SaaS / Cloud Account. Primary assets at risk: SaaS portals, Entra ID, Project platforms, Service desk, Cloud administration. Detection opportunities: SigninLogs; Impossible/unfamiliar sign-in; New SaaS access after credential exposure. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Conditional Access; Least privilege; Risk-based session controls.

data.Description: Use compromised domain credentials through VPN, Citrix or other identity-integrated internet-facing remote access. Defensive considerations: MFA; PAM/JIT; Separate remote-access groups; No standing admin remote login.

data.Name: TP-08 | Brute Force: Password Guessing

data.Description: Guess passwords against VPN, portals, administrative interfaces and web applications. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Internet-facing authentication services permit direct credential attacks, especially where MFA, throttling or lockout is weak. Applicability: Core. Internet-facing compromise phase: Guess Exposed Service Password. Primary assets at risk: VPN, Admin portal, Web login, RMM portal. Detection opportunities: Repeated failures against one account; Low-and-slow guessing. Defensive considerations: MFA; Rate limiting; Smart lockout; Strong passwords.

data.Name: TP-08 | Steal Web Session Cookie
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Steal authenticated web-session material from a browser, proxy flow or compromised web service. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Session material can bypass fresh authentication and give immediate access to exposed portals or SaaS applications. Applicability: Web / SaaS. Internet-facing compromise phase: Steal Exposed Portal Session. Primary assets at risk: Web sessions, SaaS sessions, Admin portals. Detection opportunities: Session reuse from new device/IP; Concurrent impossible session use. Defensive considerations: Token/session protection; Managed devices; Rapid revocation.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-08 | Generic System Integrator / MSP internet-facing-services profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Session material can bypass fresh authentication and give immediate access to exposed portals or SaaS applications. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to compromise of internet-facing services. Applicability=Web / SaaS; Phase=Steal Exposed Portal Session; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-08 models external reconnaissance, attack-surface discovery, exploitation of public-facing applications and edge appliances, abuse of VPN/remote access and valid public-service accounts, post-exploit command execution, web shell/server persistence, credential and token theft, privilege escalation, internal/cloud discovery, tunneling, lateral movement, data collection/exfiltration and selected service-impact actions. It is deliberately generic enough for VPNs, firewalls, web apps, APIs, project portals, Jira/Confluence-like platforms, service desks, RMM gateways and custom customer-facing applications. Product-specific CVEs are evidence/examples, not hard-coded requirements. Identity-only compromise is deeper in TP-01, trusted customer pivot in TP-03, privileged access in TP-04, software supply chain in TP-05, ransomware/destruction in TP-06 and data-theft depth in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

Detection opportunities: Token use from unusual client/IP; API calls after service exploitation. Defensive considerations: Short-lived tokens; Least privilege; Workload federation; Token rotation.

data.Name: TP-08 | Use Alternate Authentication Material: Web Session Cookie
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Replay a stolen session cookie to operate as an authenticated user or administrator. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Session replay can turn compromise of one browser or portal into valid-account access with reduced authentication friction. Applicability: Web / SaaS. Internet-facing compromise phase: Replay Stolen Portal Session. Primary assets at risk: Web portal, SaaS, Admin console. Detection opportunities: Session anomalies; New source for existing session. Defensive considerations: Session binding/token protection; Rapid revocation.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-08 | Generic System Integrator / MSP internet-facing-services profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Session replay can turn compromise of one browser or portal into valid-account access with reduced authentication friction. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to compromise of internet-facing services. Applicability=Web / SaaS; Phase=Replay Stolen Portal Session; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-08 models external reconnaissance, attack-surface discovery, exploitation of public-facing applications and edge appliances, abuse of VPN/remote access and valid public-service accounts, post-exploit command execution, web shell/server persistence, credential and token theft, privilege escalation, internal/cloud discovery, tunneling, lateral movement, data collection/exfiltration and selected service-impact actions. It is deliberately generic enough for VPNs, firewalls, web apps, APIs, project portals, Jira/Confluence-like platforms, service desks, RMM gateways and custom customer-facing applications. Product-specific CVEs are evidence/examples, not hard-coded requirements. Identity-only compromise is deeper in TP-01, trusted customer pivot in TP-03, privileged access in TP-04, software supply chain in TP-05, ransomware/destruction in TP-06 and data-theft depth in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-08 | Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Use cmd.exe or batch execution after exploiting an internet-facing Windows service. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Web exploitation often transitions immediately to native shell execution for discovery, payload transfer and persistence. Applicability: Windows Web / App. Internet-facing compromise phase: Post-Exploit Execution. Primary assets at risk: IIS/web servers, Windows application servers. Detection opportunities: w3wp/java/service process spawning cmd.exe; Suspicious command chains. Defensive considerations: EDR; Application allow-listing; Service account least privilege.

data.Name: TP-08 | Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Use PowerShell to download tooling, enumerate the host, access cloud APIs or establish persistence. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: PowerShell is a common post-exploitation mechanism on Windows application servers and can bridge local compromise into Azure/M365 administration. Applicability: Windows / Cloud. Internet-facing compromise phase: Execute PowerShell Post-Exploit. Primary assets at risk: Windows web servers, App servers, Cloud APIs. data.Description: Use sh/bash or appliance shell commands after exploitation of Linux-based web, VPN or edge systems. Detection opportunities: Web/appliance process spawning shell; Unexpected shell commands from service account. Defensive considerations: Central command/audit logs; Restrict shell access; Network isolation.

data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Use WMI for remote process execution after the attacker pivots from an exposed Windows server. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: A public web-server foothold can become an internal administration foothold if the service account or harvested credentials reach other Windows systems. Detection opportunities: WmiPrvSE remote process creation; WMI from web server. Defensive considerations: Segmentation; Restrict WMI administration; EDR.

data.Name: TP-08 | Server Software Component: vSphere Installation Bundles
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Install a malicious or modified vSphere Installation Bundle on ESXi to obtain durable hypervisor-level persistence. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Where vCenter/ESXi administration is exposed or reachable from an edge compromise, hypervisor persistence creates exceptional blast radius and weak EDR visibility. Applicability: Virtualization Admin Exposure. Internet-facing compromise phase: Persist Through vSphere / ESXi Component. Primary assets at risk: ESXi, vSphere, Virtualization management. Detection opportunities: Unexpected VIB install; Acceptance-level changes; New hypervisor component. Defensive considerations: Isolate management plane; Signed components; Monitor VIB lifecycle.

data.Name: TP-08 | Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Install a service for backdoor or tunneling execution after web-server compromise. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Services provide elevated, reboot-persistent execution and may be used to survive application restart. Applicability: Windows. Internet-facing compromise phase: Persist as Windows Service. Primary assets at risk: Windows servers. Detection opportunities: Event 7045; Service binary in unusual location. Defensive considerations: Service creation monitoring; EDR.

data.Name: TP-08 | Create Account: Local Account
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Create a local user or admin account on the compromised service host or appliance. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Local persistence avoids dependence on the original exploit and may remain unnoticed on appliances outside normal identity governance. Applicability: Server / Appliance. Internet-facing compromise phase: Create Local Backdoor Account. Primary assets at risk: Local server account, Appliance admin. Detection opportunities: New account outside provisioning; Immediate admin assignment. Defensive considerations: Central account governance; Alert on local admin creation.

data.Name: TP-08 | Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Credentials
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Add attacker-controlled credentials to an application, service principal or cloud identity recovered through the public service. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Application credentials can provide long-lived machine-to-machine access even after the vulnerable service is patched. Applicability: Cloud. Internet-facing compromise phase: Backdoor App / Service Principal. Primary assets at risk: Service principal, App registration, Automation identity. Detection opportunities: New secret/certificate after web exploit; Unexpected app credential change. Defensive considerations: Workload federation; Managed identities; Alert on credential additions.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-08 | Generic System Integrator / MSP internet-facing-services profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Application credentials can provide long-lived machine-to-machine access even after the vulnerable service is patched. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to compromise of internet-facing services. Applicability=Cloud; Phase=Backdoor App / Service Principal; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-08 models external reconnaissance, attack-surface discovery, exploitation of public-facing applications and edge appliances, abuse of VPN/remote access and valid public-service accounts, post-exploit command execution, web shell/server persistence, credential and token theft, privilege escalation, internal/cloud discovery, tunneling, lateral movement, data collection/exfiltration and selected service-impact actions. It is deliberately generic enough for VPNs, firewalls, web apps, APIs, project portals, Jira/Confluence-like platforms, service desks, RMM gateways and custom customer-facing applications. Product-specific CVEs are evidence/examples, not hard-coded requirements. Identity-only compromise is deeper in TP-01, trusted customer pivot in TP-03, privileged access in TP-04, software supply chain in TP-05, ransomware/destruction in TP-06 and data-theft depth in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-08 | Modify System Image: Downgrade System Image
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Downgrade a network device or appliance to an older vulnerable software image. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Downgrading can reintroduce exploitable flaws and defeat security improvements, providing a persistence or re-entry path. Applicability: Network / Edge Conditional. Internet-facing compromise phase: Downgrade Edge Device to Vulnerable Image. Primary assets at risk: Routers, Firewalls, VPN gateways. Detection opportunities: Unexpected firmware downgrade; Version rollback. Defensive considerations: Block unsigned/old firmware; Configuration compliance.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-08 | Generic System Integrator / MSP internet-facing-services profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Downgrading can reintroduce exploitable flaws and defeat security improvements, providing a persistence or re-entry path. Threat-led context: E d g e   P e r s i s t e n c e Applicability=Network / Edge Conditional; Phase=Downgrade Edge Device to Vulnerable Image; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-08 models external reconnaissance, attack-surface discovery, exploitation of public-facing applications and edge appliances, abuse of VPN/remote access and valid public-service accounts, post-exploit command execution, web shell/server persistence, credential and token theft, privilege escalation, internal/cloud discovery, tunneling, lateral movement, data collection/exfiltration and selected service-impact actions. It is deliberately generic enough for VPNs, firewalls, web apps, APIs, project portals, Jira/Confluence-like platforms, service desks, RMM gateways and custom customer-facing applications. Product-specific CVEs are evidence/examples, not hard-coded requirements. Identity-only compromise is deeper in TP-01, trusted customer pivot in TP-03, privileged access in TP-04, software supply chain in TP-05, ransomware/destruction in TP-06 and data-theft depth in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-08 | Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Exploit a local vulnerability on the exposed server or appliance to elevate from the web/service account to root/SYSTEM/admin. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Public-facing services often run under restricted accounts; local privilege escalation unlocks credentials, persistence and internal network administration. Applicability: Core. Internet-facing compromise phase: Exploit Local Privilege Vulnerability. Primary assets at risk: Web server, Application host, VPN appliance. Detection opportunities: Exploit chain after initial web process compromise; Kernel/service crash plus privilege change. Defensive considerations: Patch local vulnerabilities; Harden service accounts; Sandboxing.

data.Name: TP-08 | Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Bypass User Account Control
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Bypass UAC after obtaining an administrative but filtered Windows token. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This can convert a constrained application-server foothold into full local administrative execution. Applicability: Windows. Internet-facing compromise phase: Bypass UAC on Windows Server. Primary assets at risk: Windows web/application server. Detection opportunities: Known UAC bypass process chains. data.Name: TP-08 | Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Use sudo permissions or cached sudo credentials to obtain root access. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Application administrators and appliance support accounts may have sudo paths that turn a service compromise into root control. Applicability: Linux / Edge. Internet-facing compromise phase: Elevate on Linux / Appliance. Primary assets at risk: Linux server, Edge appliance. Detection opportunities: Unexpected sudo from service account; sudoers abuse. Defensive considerations: Least privilege; No passwordless broad sudo; auditd.

data.Name: TP-08 | Exploitation for Credential Access
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Exploit a vulnerability specifically to obtain credentials, tokens or authentication material from the application, appliance or operating system. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Some edge and web vulnerabilities expose session databases, configuration or credential material even without full code execution. Applicability: Core / Conditional. Internet-facing compromise phase: Exploit Service to Extract Credentials. Primary assets at risk: VPN credentials, Session data, Application secrets. Detection opportunities: Unusual credential-store access following exploit; Exploit-specific telemetry. Defensive considerations: Patch KEVs; Credential isolation; Rotate secrets after appliance compromise.

data.Name: TP-08 | OS Credential Dumping: Proc Filesystem
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Use /proc or process-memory access to recover tokens, passwords or secrets from Linux service processes. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Public web and application processes may hold database, API, SSO or cloud tokens in memory. Applicability: Linux. Internet-facing compromise phase: Read Linux Process Memory / Secrets. Primary assets at risk: Application process, Service tokens, Database credentials. Detection opportunities: Reads of /proc/<pid>/mem; ptrace by unexpected process. Defensive considerations: Process isolation; No secrets in long-lived environment; auditd.

data.Name: TP-08 | Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Query the instance metadata endpoint from a compromised cloud-hosted web application to obtain workload credentials. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: A public cloud web-service exploit can immediately become cloud-control-plane compromise if the VM/container has an over-privileged managed identity. Applicability: Cloud / IaaS. Internet-facing compromise phase: Steal Managed Identity from Public Cloud Workload. Primary assets at risk: Managed identity, Cloud VM, Application workload. Detection opportunities: Unexpected IMDS access; Token use outside normal workload behavior. Defensive considerations: Least-privileged managed identities; Harden metadata access; Workload isolation.

data.Name: TP-08 | Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-08 Internet-Facing Services Compromise
data.Description: Extract saved browser credentials and session material from an administrative or support host reached from the exposed service. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: If the public foothold reaches a jump host, cached browser credentials can reveal customer and cloud administration sessions. Applicability: Post-Pivot Conditional. Internet-facing compromise phase: Steal Browser Credentials from Admin / Jump Host. Primary assets at risk: Browser profiles, Admin workstation, Jump host. Detection opportunities: Browser credential-database access. Defensive considerations: PAW; No stored admin passwords; EDR.

data.Description: Use recovered workload/admin permissions to retrieve secrets from a cloud secret-management store. Internet-facing compromise phase: Read Cloud Secret Store. Primary assets at risk: Azure Key Vault, Cloud secrets, Certificates. Detection opportunities: Bulk secret retrieval; Secret reads after public-service exploit. Defensive considerations: Per-workload secret scope; Managed identities; PIM.

data.Description: Enumerate established connections to identify databases, identity servers, APIs and management systems. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Active service connections provide a low-noise map of the application's trusted backend relationships. Applicability: Core. Internet-facing compromise phase: Inspect Active Backend Connections. Primary assets at risk: Database servers, Internal APIs, Identity services. Detection opportunities: netstat/ss from service context. Defensive considerations: Behavior analytics.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-08 | Generic System Integrator / MSP internet-facing-services profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Description: Enumerate running processes to identify EDR, database clients, application components and privileged services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Process discovery informs defense evasion and credential targeting on web and application hosts. Applicability: Core. Internet-facing compromise phase: Identify Security / Application Processes. Primary assets at risk: EDR, Application services, Database clients. Detection opportunities: tasklist/ps from service account. Defensive considerations: Behavioral detection.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-08 | Generic System Integrator / MSP internet-facing-services profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Process discovery informs defense evasion and credential targeting on web and application hosts. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to compromise of internet-facing services. Applicability=Core; Phase=Identify Security / Application Processes; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-08 models external reconnaissance, attack-surface discovery, exploitation of public-facing applications and edge appliances, abuse of VPN/remote access and valid public-service accounts, post-exploit command execution, web shell/server persistence, credential and token theft, privilege escalation, internal/cloud discovery, tunneling, lateral movement, data collection/exfiltration and selected service-impact actions. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.
